FARRA:v2p318/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p318/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p318/r4.claim: The afterlife is حياة لا موت فيها, life with no death.
FARRA:v2p318/r4.anchor: وإن الدار الآخرة لهي الحيوان [64] حياة لا موت فيها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p366/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p366/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p366/r1.claim: Calling worldly life هذه الدنيا belittles it: because it vanishes quickly and its people die, it is like children's play for an hour before they separate.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p366/r1.anchor: وما هذه الحياة الدنيا: الإشارة بهذه ازدراء للدنيا وتصغير لأمرها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p366/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p366/r2.speaker: الخليل وسيبويه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p366/r2.claim: Al-Khalīl and Sībawayh take الحيوان as the verbal noun of حيِيَ; here it means the enduring abode of life. Mujāhid says there is no death there; another explanation calls the living person by the verbal noun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p366/r2.anchor: والحيوان، والحياة بمعنى واحد، وهو عند الخليل وسيبويه مصدر حيي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p366/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p366/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p366/r3.claim: The afterlife is called حیّاً hyperbolically for its life; فعلان marks movement and agitation, and the لو clause leaves its answer implicit: people would not choose the perishable if they knew.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p366/r3.anchor: وجعلت الدار الآخرة حيا على المبالغة بالوصف بالحياة

SAMIN-DURR:29:64/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:29:64/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:29:64/r1.claim: Some supply حياة before the subject to match it with الحيوان, but the author prefers the emphatic direct wording without that addition.
SAMIN-DURR:29:64/r1.anchor: قوله: { الحيوان }: قدر أبو البقاء وغيره قبل المبتدأ، مضافا أي: وإن حياة الدار الآخرة. وإنما قدروا ذلك

SAMIN-DURR:29:64/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:29:64/r2.speaker: سيبويه وأتباعه
SAMIN-DURR:29:64/r2.claim: Sibawayh and followers derive واو in الحيوان from ياء by anomalous replacement, as also in proper name حيوة.
SAMIN-DURR:29:64/r2.anchor: وواو " الحيوان " عن ياء عند سيبويه وأتباعه. وإنما أبدلت واوا شذوذا، وكذا في " حيوة " علما.

SAMIN-DURR:29:64/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:29:64/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:29:64/r3.claim: Abu al-Baqa says واو avoids confusion with the dual حييان; it was not changed to alif lest one of two alifs be deleted.
SAMIN-DURR:29:64/r3.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: " لئلا يلتبس بالتثنية " يعني لو قيل: حييان. قال: " ولم تقلب ألفا لتحركها وانفتاح ما قبلها

SAMIN-DURR:29:64/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:29:64/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:29:64/r4.claim: Others take the form at face value, with واو as root-final; حيي does not disprove Sibawayh because واو becomes ياء after kasra.
SAMIN-DURR:29:64/r4.anchor: وغير سيبويه حمل ذلك على ظاهره، فالحياة عنده لامها واو. ولا دليل لسيبويه في " حيي " لأن الواو متى انكسر ما قبلها

SAMIN-DURR:29:64/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:29:64/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:29:64/r5.claim: If they knew the afterlife is the true life, they would not prefer this world over it.
SAMIN-DURR:29:64/r5.anchor: قوله: { لو كانوا يعلمون } / أي: لو كانوا يعلمون أنها الحيوان لما آثروا عليها الدنيا.

ASAD-NOTES:29:62#n58/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:29:62#n58/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:29:62#n58/r1.claim: The li before yakfuru and yatarnatta'u signals a causal sequence, not purpose; Asad renders it "and thus".
ASAD-NOTES:29:62#n58/r1.anchor: is not an indication of intent ("so that" or "in order that") but merely of a causal sequence; in the above context, it may be appropriately rendered as "and thus".

ASAD-NOTES:29:63/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:29:63/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:29:63/r1.claim: Asad renders al-hayawan as the only true life, contrasting the hereafter with worldly diversion and play.
ASAD-NOTES:29:63/r1.anchor: the life in the hereafter is indeed the only [true] life: if they but knew this!

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p60/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p60/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p60/r1.claim: Qur'anic word order is deliberate: no word is advanced without a contextual purpose, and the whole expression is considered together.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p60/r1.anchor: لم يقدم لفظة على لفظة إلا لغرض يقتضيه السياق

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p60/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p60/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p60/r2.claim: The grandeur and height of Qur'anic expression show that such composition is beyond human capacity.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p60/r2.anchor: مثل هذا النظم لا يمكن أن يكون في طوق بشر فسبحان الله رب العالمين

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p60/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p60/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p60/r3.claim: Across the Qur'an play normally precedes amusement; this verse uniquely puts amusement before play.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p60/r3.anchor: كل الآيات في القرآن جاء اللعب مقدّماً على اللهو إلا في هذه الآية من سورة العنكبوت

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p60/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p60/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p60/r4.claim: The preceding verse discusses God's provision, which is associated with distraction and amusement rather than play; 63:9 likewise warns that wealth and children can distract from God's remembrance.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p60/r4.anchor: والرزق ليس من مدعاة اللعب وإنما اللهو كما في قوله تعالى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p511/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p511/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p511/r1.claim: He says every Qur’anic word is deliberately placed and its arrangement rises beyond human ability, as the examples of word order demonstrate.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p511/r1.anchor: فهي تدل دلالة واضحة على أن التعبير القرآني تعبير مقصود

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p511/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p511/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p511/r2.claim: Although other Qur’anic verses place play before amusement, 29:64 reverses the order because the preceding mention of provision relates to diversion, as money and children can divert people from remembrance.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p511/r2.anchor: والرزق ليس من مدعاة اللعب وإنما اللهو كما في قوله تعالى في سورة المنافقون

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p99#4/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p99#4/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p99#4/r1.claim: Qatada says the Hereafter is truly life.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p99#4/r1.anchor: عن قتاد ﴿ وإن الدار الآخرة لهي الحيوان ﴾ قال هي الحياة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p12#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p12#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p12#2/r1.claim: Calling this life worldly signals its contemptibility; with God it is worth less than a mosquito's wing.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p12#2/r1.anchor: هذه الحياة الدنيا ( إشارة تحقير وكيف لا والدنيا لا تزن عند الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v21p12#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p12#2/r2.speaker: سهل بن سعد
ALUSI-FULL:v21p12#2/r2.claim: Al-Tirmidhī reports from Sahl ibn Saʿd that the Prophet said, if the world weighed a mosquito's wing with God, no disbeliever would receive a drink of water from it.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p12#2/r2.anchor: عن سهل بن سعد قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم لو كانت الدنيا تعدل

ALUSI-FULL:v21p12#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p12#2/r3.speaker: بعض العارفين
ALUSI-FULL:v21p12#2/r3.claim: Some gnostics describe the world as more contemptible than a cubit's length of dead pig on which a dog urinated, held by a leper.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p12#2/r3.anchor: وقال بعض العارفين : الدنيا أحقر من ذراع خنزير ميت بال عليها كلب

ALUSI-FULL:v21p12#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p12#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p12#2/r4.claim: Worldly life is like children's amusement: they gather around it and rejoice briefly, then disperse; this is an eloquent condensed simile.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p12#2/r4.anchor: أي إلا كما يلهو ويلعب به الصبيان يجتمعون عليه ويبتهجون به ساعة ثم يتفرقون عنه وهذا من التشبيه البليغ

ALUSI-FULL:v21p12#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p12#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p12#2/r5.claim: The afterlife is the true abode of life, where its people face no death or extinction; alternatively, it is itself life, for emphasis.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p12#2/r5.anchor: أي لهي دار الحياة الحقيقية إذ لا يعرض الموت والفناء لمن فيها أو هي ذاتها حياة للمبالغة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p12#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p12#2/r6.speaker: سيبويه
ALUSI-FULL:v21p12#2/r6.claim: Alusi explains al-ḥayawān as a verbal noun used for a living being, originally ḥayayan; the second yāʾ became wāw anomalously, leaving yāʾ as the final root letter, as Sībawayh holds.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p12#2/r6.anchor: مصدر حي سمي به ذو الحياة في غير هذا المحل وأصله حييان فقلبت الثانية ولوا على خلاف القياس فلامه ياء وإلى ذلك ذهب سيبويه

ALUSI-FULL:v21p12#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p12#2/r7.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v21p12#2/r7.claim: An alternative says the final root letter is wāw, following the word's apparent form and the proper name Ḥayāt.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p12#2/r7.anchor: قيل : إن لامه واو نظرا إلى ظاهر الكلمة وإلى حياة علم رجل

ALUSI-FULL:v21p12#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p12#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p12#2/r8.claim: The form ḥayy does not prove a yāʾ root, since wāw can turn into yāʾ after a preceding kasra, as in shaqiya from shaqwa.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p12#2/r8.anchor: ولا حجة على كونه ياء في حي لأن الواو في مثله تبدل ياء لكسر ما قبلها نحو شقي من الشقوة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p12#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p12#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p12#2/r9.claim: The faʿalān pattern is stronger than plain life because it evokes the movement and agitation inherent in life, suiting the emphatic contrast with worldly life.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p12#2/r9.anchor: وهو أبلغ من الحياة لما في بناء فعلان من معنى الحركة والاضطراب اللازم للحياة ولذلك أختير عليها في هذا المقام

ALUSI-FULL:v21p12#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p12#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p12#2/r10.claim: The conditional has an omitted answer: if they knew, they would not prefer worldly existence, whose life is incidental, brief, and rapidly passing away.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p12#2/r10.anchor: شرط جوابه محذوف أي لو كانوا يعلمون لما أروا عليها الدنيا التي أصلها عدم الحياة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p12#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p12#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p12#2/r11.claim: Reading law here as an optative is unlikely.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p255/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p255/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p255/r1.claim: Leisure is enjoyment of worldly pleasures and play is frivolity; the world is called these because it is transient.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p255/r1.anchor: اللهو هو: الاستمتاع بلذات الدنيا، واللعب: العبث، سميت بهما لأنها فانية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p255/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p255/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p255/r2.claim: Al-hayawan means life: the afterlife contains enduring, permanent life.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p255/r2.anchor: أي: الحياة الدائمة الباقية، و"الحيوان": بمعنى الحياة، أي: فيها الحياة الدائمة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p255/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p255/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p255/r3.claim: If they knew, they would recognize that this world perishes and the afterlife remains.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p255/r3.anchor: {لو كانوا يعلمون} فناء الدنيا وبقاء الآخرة

BAYDAWI-FULL:29:64-65/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:64-65/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:64-65/r1.claim: Calling this life insignificant expresses contempt; with God it weighs less than a mosquito's wing.
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:64-65/r1.anchor: إشارة تحقير وكيف لا وهي لا تزن عند الله

BAYDAWI-FULL:29:64-65/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:64-65/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:64-65/r2.claim: Worldly life resembles children's play: they gather and enjoy it briefly, then part exhausted.
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:64-65/r2.anchor: إلا كما يلهى ويلعب به الصبيان

BAYDAWI-FULL:29:64-65/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:64-65/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:64-65/r3.claim: The afterlife is true life because death cannot reach it, or it is life itself by an intensive expression.
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:64-65/r3.anchor: لهي دار الحياة الحقيقية لامتناع طريان الموت عليها

BAYDAWI-FULL:29:64-65/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:64-65/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:64-65/r4.claim: Ḥayawān is a verbal noun of ḥayya used for a living being; originally ḥayayan, its second yāʾ changed to wāw.
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:64-65/r4.anchor: { الحيوان } مصدر حي سمي به ذو الحياة

BAYDAWI-FULL:29:64-65/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:64-65/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:64-65/r5.claim: Ḥayawān is more emphatic than ḥayāh because faʿalān suggests life's movement and agitation.
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:64-65/r5.anchor: وهو أبلغ من الحياة لما في بناء فعلان من الحركة

BAYDAWI-FULL:29:64-65/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:64-65/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:64-65/r6.claim: If they knew, they would not prefer worldly life, whose life is incidental, brief, and rooted in nonlife.
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:64-65/r6.anchor: لم يؤثروا عليها الدنيا التي أصلها عدم الحياة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p576/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p576/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p576/r1.claim: The preceding verses establish that worldly life is perishing and transient, so treating it as a source of lasting joy is misplaced.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p576/r1.anchor: ولما تبين بهذا الآيات أن الدنيا مبنية على الفناء والزوال

BIQAI-FULL:v5p576/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p576/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p576/r2.claim: The demonstrative belittles worldly life; calling it the lower life itself supports acknowledgment of the afterlife.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p576/r2.anchor: فحقرها بالإشارة ولفظ الدناءة مع الإشارة إلى أن الاعتراف بهذا الاسم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p576/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p576/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p576/r3.claim: Because the sura urges striving and forbids wrongdoing, the verse mentions diversion first: turning away from it cuts off a source of evil.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p576/r3.anchor: ولما كان مقصود السورة الحث على الجهاد والنهي عن المنكر , وكان في معرض

BIQAI-FULL:v5p576/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p576/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p576/r4.claim: Lahw is anything that distracts from benefit, such as singing or the adornment of wealth and women, which pleases and excites the soul.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p576/r4.anchor: فإن اللهو كل شيء من شأنه أن يعجب النفس

BIQAI-FULL:v5p576/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p576/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p576/r5.claim: Diversion causes heedlessness, forgetfulness, and neglect of reason and what saves one in the afterlife, leading to misguidance; Biqaʿi links this to 31:6.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p576/r5.anchor: فيكون سببا للغفلة والذهول والنسيان والشغل

BIQAI-FULL:v5p577/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p577/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p577/r1.claim: Laʿib gives worldly pleasure, such as dancing after listening; it quickly vanishes because it opposes seriousness and resembles jest.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p577/r1.anchor: وهو فعل ما يزيد النفس في دنياها سرورا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p577/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p577/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p577/r2.claim: Play can mean anything low or false used for amusement and passing time; laʿba can mean a figurine or toy such as chess, and the verb can mean frolicking or treating religion lightly.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p577/r2.anchor: وكل باطل يقصد به زيادة البسط والترويح والتمادي

BIQAI-FULL:v5p577/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p577/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p577/r3.claim: The afterlife alone is complete and enduring life, free of death and extinction; al-ḥayawān is an intensive form.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p577/r3.anchor: أي الحياة التامة الباقية العامة الوافية نفسها

BIQAI-FULL:v5p577/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p577/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p577/r4.claim: The intensified form and its vowel suggest the movement and agitation inherent in life.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p577/r4.anchor: ولذلك اختير هذا البناء الدال على المبالغة , وحركته مشعرة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p577/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p577/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p577/r5.claim: Hereafter pleasures do not end or have low motives; they consist in glorification, knowledge, ease, expansion, intimacy, and delight.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p577/r5.anchor: بل كان ذلك بالتسبيح والتقديس وما يترتب عليه من المعارف

BIQAI-FULL:v5p577/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p577/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p577/r6.claim: People mistake both abodes, treating worldly life as permanent and the afterlife as nonexistent, though this world began without life and is mortal.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p577/r6.anchor: فأنزلوا كل واحدة منهما غير منزلتها

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3080#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3080#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3080#3/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the present world is one week of the Hereafter, lasting seven thousand years; 6,200 years had passed, and the world would end with no monotheist on it.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3080#3/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : الدنيا جمعة من جمع الاخرة سبعة الاف سنة ، فقد مضا منها ستة الالف ومائتين من سنين

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3080#3/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3080#3/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3080#3/r2.claim: Mujahid glosses amusement as the drum.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3080#3/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد قال : اللهو : هو الطبل

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3080#3/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3080#3/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3080#3/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas explains amusement here as play.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3080#3/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس : قوله : لهو يقول : لعبا

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3080#3/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3080#3/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3080#3/r4.claim: Mujahid also glosses amusement as falsehood.

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3080#3/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3080#3/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3080#3/r5.claim: Mujahid says that every kind of play is amusement.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3080#3/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد قال : كل لعب لهو

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3080#3/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3080#3/r6.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3080#3/r6.claim: Ibn Umar identifies the Hereafter abode as Paradise.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3080#3/r6.anchor: عن ابن عمر قوله : الدار الاخرة يقول : الجنة

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3080#3/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3080#3/r7.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3080#3/r7.claim: Al-Dahhak explains the Hereafter as everlasting life.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3080#3/r7.anchor: عن الضحاك ان الدار الاخرة لهي الحيوان قال : الحياة الدائمة

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3080#3/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3080#3/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3080#3/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Hereafter is enduring.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3080#3/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس لهي الحيوان يقول : باقية

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3080#3/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3080#3/r9.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3080#3/r9.claim: Mujahid says there is no death in the Hereafter.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3080#3/r9.anchor: عن مجاهد وان الدار الاخرة لهي الحيوان لا موت فيها

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3080#3/r10.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3080#3/r10.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3080#3/r10.claim: Qatada likewise glosses the Hereafter as life without death.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3080#3/r10.anchor: عن قتادة وان الدار الاخرة لهي الحيوان لو كانوا يعلمون حياة لا موت فيها

BURSEVI:v6p356/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p356/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p356/r1.claim: The afterlife is Paradise, the true abode of life because death and extinction cannot reach it; alternatively, it is itself life, an emphatic usage.
BURSEVI:v6p356/r1.anchor: أي : الجنة لهي دار الحياة الحقيقية لامتناع طريان الموت والفناء عليها أو هي في ذاتها حياة للمبالغة

BURSEVI:v6p356/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p356/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p356/r2.claim: Ḥayawān is a verbal noun from ḥayiya, used for a living being; its original form was ḥayyān, altered to avoid dropping one of the two alifs.
BURSEVI:v6p356/r2.anchor: والحيوان مصدر حيي سمي به ذو الحياة وأصله حييان فقلبت الياء الثانية واوا لئلا يحذف إحدى الألفات

BURSEVI:v6p356/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p356/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p356/r3.claim: Ḥayawān is more emphatic than ḥayāh because the faʿalān pattern conveys motion and agitation, fitting this context of emphasis.
BURSEVI:v6p356/r3.anchor: وهو أبلغ من الحياة لما في بناء فعلان من الحركة والاضطراب اللازم للحيوان ولذلك اختير على الحياة

BURSEVI:v6p356/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p356/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p356/r4.claim: If people understood, they would not prefer worldly life, whose basis is lifelessness and whose life is only a brief, vanishing accident.
BURSEVI:v6p356/r4.anchor: لما آثروا عليها الدنيا التي أصلها عدم الحياة ثم ما يحدث فيها من الحياة عارضة سريعة الزوال

BURSEVI:v6p356/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p356/r5.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v6p356/r5.claim: The world is mortality: God calls a disbeliever dead despite being alive; only one whom He revives with faith’s light is truly living.
BURSEVI:v6p356/r5.anchor: يشير إلى أن دار الدنيا لهي الموتان لأنه تعالى سمى الكافر وإن كان حيا بالميت

BURSEVI:v6p356/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p356/r6.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v6p356/r6.claim: The afterlife is the realm of spirits and the unseen kingdom, wholly alive; all its parts are living, hence it is called ḥayawān.
BURSEVI:v6p356/r6.anchor: الآخرة عبارة عن عالم الأرواح والملكوت فهي حياة كلها وإنما سماها الحيوان

BURSEVI:v6p356/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p356/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p356/r7.claim: A hadith says everything in Paradise, including its trees, fruit, rooms, walls, rivers, soil, and pebbles, is alive.
BURSEVI:v6p356/r7.anchor: إن الجنة بما فيها من الأشجار والثمار والغرف والحيطان والأنهار حتى ترابها وحصاها كلها حي

BURSEVI:v6p356/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p356/r8.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v6p356/r8.claim: Paradise offers true life untouched by distress, calamity, illness, or death; knowing its worth would make people strive harder for it here.
BURSEVI:v6p356/r8.anchor: فالحياة الحقيقية التي لا تشينها الغصص والمحن والأمراض والعلل ولا يدكها الموت والفوت لهي حياة أهل الجنات والقربات

BURSEVI:v6p356/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p356/r9.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v6p356/r9.claim: What one misses of that life here cannot be recovered in the afterlife; the people of Hell neither truly live nor find the death they wish for.
BURSEVI:v6p356/r9.anchor: فمن فاتته لا يدركها في الآخرة ألا ترى أن من صفة أهل النار أن لا يموت فيها ولا يحيا

BURSEVI:v6p356/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p356/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p356/r10.claim: Kashf al-asrar appends a Persian poem illustrating worldly striving through shifting images of a lion, wolf, partridge, and deer.
BURSEVI:v6p356/r10.anchor: غافل بي حاصل تاشند شربت مرادى آميزي ووتاكي ارزوي زي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p325/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p325/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p325/r1.claim: Worldly pursuits beyond what sustains life and strength for obedience are diversion and play; what is done for God belongs to the afterlife.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p325/r1.anchor: فأما ما كان لله فهو من الآخرة، وأما أمور الدنيا التي هي زائدة على الضروري

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p325/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p325/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p325/r2.claim: Rich and poor share the same necessities: breathing, relieving hunger, covering nakedness, and protection from heat and cold.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p325/r2.anchor: وانظر أن حالة الغني والفقير في الأمور الضرورية واحدة كالتنفس في الهواء وسد الجوع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p325/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p325/r3.speaker: الخليل وسيبويه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p325/r3.claim: Al-Khalīl and Sībawayh treat ḥayawān as a verbal noun synonymous with ḥayāh, like hayamān.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p325/r3.anchor: وهو عند الخليل وسيبويه مصدر كالهيمان ونحوه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p325/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p325/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p325/r4.claim: Mujāhid explains the afterlife as a life with no death; Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls this good.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p325/r4.anchor: والمعنى لا موت فيها قاله مجاهد وهو حسن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p283#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p283#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p283#2/r1.claim: Worldly life is a deception that passes away shortly.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p283#2/r1.anchor: والمعنى وما الحياة في هذه الدنيا إلا غرور ينقضي عن قليل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p283#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p283#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p283#2/r2.claim: The Hereafter means Paradise, the abode of life without death or the defects that accompany worldly life.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p283#2/r2.anchor: يعني الجنة لهي الحيوان قال أبو عبيدة اللام في لهي زائدة للتوكيد والحيوان والحياة واحد والمعنى لهي دار الحياة التي لا موت فيها ولا تنفيص يشوبها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p283#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p283#2/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p283#2/r3.claim: Abū ʿUbayda regards the lām in lahiya as an extra particle of emphasis.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p283#2/r3.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة اللام في لهي زائدة للتوكيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p283#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p283#2/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p283#2/r4.claim: Abū ʿUbayda says ḥayawān and ḥayāh both mean life.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p283#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p283#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p283#2/r5.claim: If they knew, they would turn from the perishing thing toward what endures; they do not know.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p283#2/r5.anchor: لو علموا لرغبوا عن الفاني في الباقي ولكنهم لا يعلمون

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p294#3/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p294#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p294#3/r1.claim: The worldly life is trivial, passing, and short-lived; the Hereafter is the real, enduring life that never ends.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p294#3/r1.anchor: يقول تعالى مخبرا عن حقارة الدنيا وزوالها وانقضائها، وأنها لا دوام لها، وغاية ما فيها لهو ولعب: {وإن الدار الآخرة لهي الحيوان}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p294#3/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p294#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p294#3/r2.claim: If people understood, they would choose what remains over what perishes.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p294#3/r2.anchor: أي: لآثروا ما يبقى على ما يفنى.

JISHUMI:v8p5590/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5590/r10.speaker: أبو عبيدة
JISHUMI:v8p5590/r10.claim: Abu Ubayda says al-hayawān and al-ḥayāh both mean life and are verbal nouns of ḥayya.
JISHUMI:v8p5590/r10.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: الحيوان والحياة واحد، وهما مصدران حيي حياة وحيوانا

JISHUMI:v8p5590/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5590/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5590/r11.claim: Life is an accident that unifies the parts of a thing so it can be knowing and powerful; its defining property is perception.
JISHUMI:v8p5590/r11.anchor: والحياة عرض يصير الأجزاء بمنزلة الشيء الواحد حتى يصحح كونه عالما قادرا، وخاصية الحياة الإدراك

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p293/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p293/r1.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p293/r1.claim: Al-Dahhak says the afterlife is the enduring life.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p293/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p293/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p293/r2.claim: Abu Ubayda says ḥayawān and ḥayāt both mean life.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p293/r2.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة : الحيوان والحياة واحد

MUJAHID:v2p497#4/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p497#4/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p497#4/r1.claim: Mujahid says the abode of the Hereafter is a life in which there is no death.
MUJAHID:v2p497#4/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ وإن الدار الآخرة لهي الحيوان ﴾ يقول لا موت فيها

MUQATIL:29:64-68/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:29:64-68/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:29:64-68/r1.claim: Worldly life is only falsehood, pastime, and play.
MUQATIL:29:64-68/r1.anchor: وما هذه الحياة الدنيآ إلا لهو ولعب } يعنى وباطلا

MUQATIL:29:64-68/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:29:64-68/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:29:64-68/r2.claim: The hereafter is Paradise, the home of real life where there is no death.
MUQATIL:29:64-68/r2.anchor: وإن الدار الآخرة } يعنى الجنة { لهي الحيوان } يقول: لهى دار الحياة لا موت فيها

NASAFI-FULL:v3p265/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p265/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p265/r1.claim: Because it passes quickly and people die away from it, worldly life is like children playing briefly and scattering; this belittles its worth.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p265/r1.anchor: أى وما هى لسرعة زوالها عن أهلها وموتهم عنها إلا كما يلعب الصبيان ساعة ثم يتفرقون وفيه ازدراء بالدنيا وتصغير لأمرها

NASAFI-FULL:v3p265/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p265/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p265/r2.claim: Lahw is a pleasure that distracts someone briefly and then ends.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p265/r2.anchor: واللهو ما يتلذذ به الإنسان فيلهيه ساعة ثم ينقضى

NASAFI-FULL:v3p265/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p265/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p265/r3.claim: The world is so slight that, with God, it does not weigh a mosquito's wing.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p265/r3.anchor: وهى لا تزن عنده جناح بعوضة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p265/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p265/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p265/r4.claim: Al-hayawan means life: the next abode has continuous life with no death, as though life were its essence.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p265/r4.anchor: أى الحياة ليس فيها إلا حياة مستمرة دائمة لا موت فيها فكانها فى ذاتها حياة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p265/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p265/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p265/r5.claim: Hayawan is the verbal noun of hayy; its expected form is hayayan, with the second ya changed to waw.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p265/r5.anchor: والحيوان مصدر حى وقياسه حييان فقلبت الياء الثانية واوا

NASAFI-FULL:v3p265/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p265/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p265/r6.claim: Hayawan replaces hayat because faʿalan conveys motion and agitation, matching life as motion and death as stillness, and intensifies life.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p265/r6.anchor: ولم يقل لهى الحياة لما فى بناء فعلان من معنى الحركة والاضطراب والحياة حركة والموت سكون فمجيئه على بناء دال على معنى الحركة مبالغة معنى الحياة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p265/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p265/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p265/r7.claim: Pause at al-hayawan: connecting the next clause would make the afterlife's being life depend on their knowing, which it does not.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p265/r7.anchor: ويوقف على الحيوان لأن التقدير ﴿ لو كانوا يعلمون ﴾ حقيقة الدارين

NASAFI-FULL:v3p265/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p265/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p265/r8.claim: If they knew the nature of both abodes, they would not prefer fleeting amusement to lasting life.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p265/r8.anchor: حقيقة الدارين لما اختاروا اللهو الفانى على الحيوان الباقى

QURTUBI-FULL:29:63-64/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:63-64/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:29:63-64/r6.claim: Worldly life is diversion and play: wealth and status fade and have no enduring reality, like play that does not last.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:63-64/r6.anchor: ليس ما أعطاه الله الأغنياء من الدنيا إلا وهو يضمحل ويزول كاللعب الذي لا حقيقة له ولا ثبات

QURTUBI-FULL:29:63-64/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:63-64/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:29:63-64/r7.claim: This criticism concerns worldly wealth, status, and clothing beyond basic needs and the means needed to sustain life and obey God.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:63-64/r7.anchor: الملبس الزائد على الضروري الذي به قوام العيش

QURTUBI-FULL:29:63-64/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:63-64/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:29:63-64/r8.claim: What is done for God belongs to the afterlife and endures, meaning what is sought for His reward and pleasure.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:63-64/r8.anchor: أي ما ابتغى به ثوابه ورضاه

QURTUBI-FULL:29:63-64/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:63-64/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:29:63-64/r9.claim: The afterlife is the lasting abode of life: it does not pass away and contains no death.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:63-64/r9.anchor: أي دار الحياة الباقية التي لا تزول ولا موت فيها

QURTUBI-FULL:29:63-64/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:63-64/r10.speaker: أبو عبيدة
QURTUBI-FULL:29:63-64/r10.claim: Abu Ubayda equates al-ḥayawān with life and the word ḥayy with a kasra; an anonymous poetic line illustrates the usage of ḥayāt.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:63-64/r10.anchor: وزعم أبو عبيدة: أن الحيوان والحياة والحي بكسر الحاء واحد

QURTUBI-FULL:29:63-64/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:63-64/r11.speaker: غيره
QURTUBI-FULL:29:63-64/r11.claim: Others explain ḥayy as a plural on the pattern fuʿūl, like ʿuṣiyy.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:63-64/r11.anchor: وغيره يقول: إن الحي جمع على فعول مثل عصي

QURTUBI-FULL:29:63-64/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:63-64/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:29:63-64/r12.claim: The word al-ḥayawān can refer to any living thing.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:63-64/r12.anchor: والحيوان يقع على كل شيء حي

QURTUBI-FULL:29:63-64/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:63-64/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:29:63-64/r13.claim: The commentary also notes that Ḥayawān is the name of a spring in Paradise.

QURTUBI-FULL:29:63-64/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:63-64/r14.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:29:63-64/r14.claim: One derivation makes ḥayawān originally ḥayayyān, with one yāʾ changed to wāw where identical letters meet.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:63-64/r14.anchor: وقيل: أصل حيوان حييان فأبدلت إحداهما واوا لاجتماع المثلين

QURTUBI-FULL:29:63-64/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:63-64/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:29:63-64/r15.claim: The closing clause means that they would know the afterlife is truly the enduring life if they understood.

RAZI-FULL:v25p80/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p80/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p80/r1.claim: Because people acknowledge God as creator and provider yet leave worship for worldly adornment, al-Razi says God shows that what attracts them is nothing.
RAZI-FULL:v25p80/r1.anchor: لما بين أنهم يعترفون بكون الله هو الخالق وكونه هو الرزاق وهم يتركون عبادته ولا يتركونها إلا لزينة الحياة الدنيا

RAZI-FULL:v25p80/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p80/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p80/r2.claim: One distinction is that play means turning toward falsehood for fleeting pleasure, while lahw means turning away from truth; worldly life involves both.
RAZI-FULL:v25p80/r2.anchor: فالإقبال على الباطل لعب والإعراض عن الحق لهو

RAZI-FULL:v25p80/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p80/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p80/r3.claim: Alternatively, play is putting one activity first and intending to do the other later, while lahw is becoming absorbed in one and turning wholly from the other.
RAZI-FULL:v25p80/r3.anchor: فالأول لعب والثاني لهو ، والدليل عليه هو أن الشطرنج والحمام وغيرهما

RAZI-FULL:v25p80/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p80/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p80/r4.claim: Chess and pigeon keeping are not conventionally called instruments of lahw, but stringed instruments are because their immediate pleasure distracts a person from everything else.
RAZI-FULL:v25p80/r4.anchor: والعود وغيره من الأوتار تسمى آلات الملاهي لأنها تلهي الإنسان عن غيرها لما فيها من اللذة الحالية

RAZI-FULL:v25p80/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p80/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p80/r5.claim: For some people worldly life is play: they engage in it expecting to turn to worship and the afterlife later; for others it is lahw, and they forget the afterlife entirely.
RAZI-FULL:v25p80/r5.anchor: فالدنيا للبعض لعب يشتغل به ويقول بعد هذا الشغل أشتغل بالعبادة والآخرة ، وللبعض لهو يشتغل به

RAZI-FULL:v25p80/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p80/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p80/r6.claim: The demonstrative “this” fits the present context because it has just mentioned worldly life through the earth revived by rain; in the cited regret passage, the preceding scene is the afterlife, so it says simply “worldly life.”
RAZI-FULL:v25p80/r6.anchor: لأن المذكور من قبل ههنا أمر الدنيا

RAZI-FULL:v25p80#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p80#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p80#2/r1.claim: The order reverses “play and lahw” in the regret passage: there, absorption in worldly life is remote; here, worldly life’s attraction makes absorption more likely, so lahw comes first.
RAZI-FULL:v25p80#2/r1.anchor: فنقول لما كان المذكور هناك من قبل الآخرة وإظهارهم للحسرة ، ففي ذلك الوقت يبعد الاستغراق

RAZI-FULL:v25p80#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p80#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p80#2/r2.claim: The regret passage only needs to say the afterlife is better, but people absorbed in worldly life need the stronger warning that real life is only in the afterlife.
RAZI-FULL:v25p80#2/r2.anchor: ولما كان ههنا الحال حال الاشتغال بالدنيا احتاج إلى رادع قوي فقال لا حياة إلا حياة الآخرة

RAZI-FULL:v25p80#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p80#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p80#2/r3.claim: Al-Razi omits “for those who fear God” here because only the God-fearing find the afterlife better, whereas its lasting, eternal life is not restricted to one group.
RAZI-FULL:v25p80#2/r3.anchor: لأن الآخرة خير للمتقي فحسب أي المتقي عن الشرك

RAZI-FULL:v25p80#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p80#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p80#2/r4.claim: Al-ḥayawān is a verbal noun from ḥayya, like ḥayāh, but carries greater emphasis; the afterlife is the second and truly substantial life.
RAZI-FULL:v25p80#2/r4.anchor: الحيوان مصدر حي كالحياة لكن فيها مبالغة ليست في الحياة والمراد بالدار الآخرة هي الحياة الثانية

RAZI-FULL:v25p80#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p80#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p80#2/r5.claim: Alternatively, the afterlife earns this name because it contains increase and growth and is where full, true perception occurs.
RAZI-FULL:v25p80#2/r5.anchor: لما كانت الآخرة فيها الزيادة والنمو كما قال تعالى

STUDYQURAN:29:64/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:29:64/r1.speaker: Aj
STUDYQURAN:29:64/r1.claim: The world's play and diversion indicate how rapidly it dissipates.
STUDYQURAN:29:64/r1.anchor: indicating the rapidity with which it dissipates (Aj)

STUDYQURAN:29:64/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:29:64/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:29:64/r2.claim: The world is also called an enjoyment of delusion at 3:185.
STUDYQURAN:29:64/r2.anchor: as naught but the enjoyment of delusion (3:185)

STUDYQURAN:29:64/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:29:64/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:29:64/r3.claim: Verse 57:20 further describes worldly life as play, diversion, glitter, boasting, and competition for wealth and children, comparing it to vegetation that withers into chaff.
STUDYQURAN:29:64/r3.anchor: a rain whose vegetation impresses the farmers; then it withers such that you see it turn yellow; then it becomes chaff

STUDYQURAN:29:64/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:29:64/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:29:64/r4.claim: The Abode of the Hereafter refers to Paradise.

TAB-FULL:v18p440/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p440/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p440/r1.claim: Worldly life is amusement and play: people gratify themselves with pleasures that soon end and have no permanence.
TAB-FULL:v18p440/r1.anchor: إلا تعليل النفوس بما تلتذ به، ثم هو منقض عن قريب، لا بقاء له ولا دوام

TAB-FULL:v18p440/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p440/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p440/r2.claim: The afterlife contains enduring life without disappearance, interruption, or death.
TAB-FULL:v18p440/r2.anchor: وإن الدار الآخرة لفيها الحياة الدائمة التي لا زوال لها، ولا انقطاع، ولا موت معها

TAB-FULL:v18p440/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p440/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p440/r3.claim: Qatāda glosses the afterlife’s life as life without death.
TAB-FULL:v18p440/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: " {وإن الدار الآخرة لهي الحيوان لو كانوا يعلمون}

TAB-FULL:v18p440/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p440/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v18p440/r4.claim: Mujāhid likewise says there is no death in the afterlife.

TAB-FULL:v18p440/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p440/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p440/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains that the afterlife remains.
TAB-FULL:v18p440/r5.anchor: عن علي، عن ابن عباس، في قوله " {وإن الدار الآخرة لهي الحيوان}

TABATABAI:29:61-69/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:61-69/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:61-69/r2.claim: لهو is what distracts and occupies someone from what matters; worldly life distracts people from lasting life through its fading attractions.
TABATABAI:29:61-69/r2.anchor: اللهو ما يلهيك ويشغلك عما يهمك فالحياة الدنيا من اللهو

TABATABAI:29:61-69/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:61-69/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:61-69/r3.claim: لعب is an arrangement of actions for an imaginary end, like children’s play; worldly life is play because it quickly vanishes like a children’s game.
TABATABAI:29:61-69/r3.anchor: اللعب فعل أو أفعال منتظمة انتظاما خياليا لغاية خيالية كملاعب الصبيان

TABATABAI:29:61-69/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:61-69/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:61-69/r4.claim: The objects people compete and oppress over—wealth, spouses, children, rank, leadership, servants, and supporters—are illusory possessions held only in imagination.
TABATABAI:29:61-69/r4.anchor: عامة المقاصد التي يتنافس فيها المتنافسون ويتكالب عليه الظالمون أمور وهمية سرابية

TABATABAI:29:61-69/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:61-69/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:61-69/r5.claim: The afterlife is real, complete life acquired through faith and good works: lasting, free from play, pain, misery, nonsense, and sin.
TABATABAI:29:61-69/r5.anchor: وأما الحياة الآخرة التي يعيش فيها الإنسان بكماله الواقعي الذي اكتسبه بإيمانه وعمله الصالح

TABATABAI:29:61-69/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:61-69/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:61-69/r6.claim: The verse belittles this life with “this,” restricts it to amusement and play, and emphatically restricts the afterlife to true life using إن, the lām, separation pronoun, and nominal form.
TABATABAI:29:61-69/r6.anchor: قصر الحياة الدنيا في اللهو واللعب والإشارة إليها بهذه المفيدة للتحقير

TABATABAI:29:61-69/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:61-69/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:61-69/r7.claim: “If they knew” means that, if they had knowledge, they would recognize the truth of this description.
TABATABAI:29:61-69/r7.anchor: أي لو كانوا يعلمون لعلموا أن الأمر كما وصفنا

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p339#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p339#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p339#2/r1.claim: Al-ḥayawān means the abode of life: Paradise, where there is no death.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p339#2/r1.anchor: وإن الدار الآخرة لهي الحيوان} يعني: الجنة هي دار الحياة؛ أي لا موت فيها.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p555#3/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p555#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p555#3/r1.claim: Worldly life here is false, delusive, and idle, soon to pass away.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p555#3/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومقاتل: يريد باطل وغرور وعبث تنقضي عن قريب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p555#3/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p555#3/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p555#3/r2.claim: The Hereafter is the abode of life in which its inhabitants do not die.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p555#3/r2.anchor: وقال الكلبي: هي حياة لا يموت فيها أهلها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p555#3/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p555#3/r3.speaker: قتادة والسدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p555#3/r3.claim: Qatāda and al-Suddī gloss al-ḥayawān as life.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p555#3/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p555#3/r4.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p555#3/r4.claim: Al-Farrāʾ explains it as life without death.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p555#3/r4.anchor: وقال الفراء: لهي الحياة حياة لا موت فيها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p555#3/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p555#3/r5.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p555#3/r5.claim: Al-Zajjāj says it means the enduring abode of life.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p555#3/r5.anchor: وقال الزجاج: معناه: هي دار الحياة الدائمة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p555#3/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p555#3/r6.speaker: أبو عبيدة وابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p555#3/r6.claim: Abū ʿUbayda and Ibn Qutayba say al-ḥayawān means life; exegetes and semantic scholars agree on that sense here.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p555#3/r6.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة وابن قتيبة: {الحيوان} الحياة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p555#3/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p555#3/r7.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p555#3/r7.claim: Reporting Abū ʿUbayda, Abū ʿAlī says al-ḥayāt, al-ḥayawān, and al-ḥayy are verbal nouns.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p555#3/r7.anchor: قال أبو علي: قال أبو عبيدة: الحياة والحيوان والحي واحد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p555#3/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p555#3/r8.speaker: أبو زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p555#3/r8.claim: Abū Zayd says ḥayawān can mean any animate thing, the opposite of lifeless matter; it may be an adjective rather than a verbal noun.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p555#3/r8.anchor: وقال أبو زيد: الحيوان ما فيه روح

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p555#3/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p555#3/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p555#3/r9.claim: Al-ḥayawān may be a verbal noun per Abū ʿUbayda or an adjective per Abū Zayd, comparable to ṣamiyān and zafiyān.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p555#3/r9.anchor: والحيوان في روايتي أبي زيد وأبي عبيدة على ضربين؛ أحدهما: أن يكون مصدرا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p555#3/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p555#3/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p555#3/r10.claim: The poem's zafiyān witnesses an adjectival pattern like ṣamiyān, supporting the adjective analysis.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p555#3/r10.anchor: فهذا أظهر من أن يقال له وصف بالمصدر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p555#3/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p555#3/r11.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p555#3/r11.claim: As a verbal noun, the phrase means the Hereafter's life is true life, without the deficiency and ending that mar worldly life.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p555#3/r11.anchor: فيحتمل أن يكون المعنى: وإن حياة الدار الآخرة هي الحياة؛ لأنه لا نقص فيها ولا نفاد لها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p555#3/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p555#3/r12.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p555#3/r12.claim: Alternatively, the Hereafter is called living because it neither vanishes nor perishes; the description refers to its inhabitants.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p555#3/r12.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الحيوان الذي هو خلاف الموتان، وقيل للدار الآخرة: الحيوان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p558/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p558/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p558/r1.claim: The phrase can mean the Hereafter is the abode possessing life, as if worldly life did not count as life.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p558/r1.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون التقدير في قوله: {لهي الحيوان} هي ذات الحيوان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p558/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p558/r2.speaker: الخليل وسيبويه وأصحابهما
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p558/r2.claim: Al-Khalīl, Sībawayh, and their colleagues derive the wāw by changing the second of two root yāʾs, since this pattern does not allow assimilation.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p558/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p558/r3.speaker: أبو عثمان
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p558/r3.claim: Abū ʿUthmān says the wāw is original and al-ḥayawān is a verbal noun without a corresponding verb, like fawẓ.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p558/r3.anchor: إلا أبا عثمان فإنه ذهب في أن الحيوان غير مبدل الواو

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p558/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p558/r4.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p558/r4.claim: Abū ʿAlī rejects Abū ʿUthmān's analogy: words with medial wāw and a sound final exist, but the proposed yāʾ-medial, wāw-final pattern does not.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p558/r4.anchor: قال أبو علي: الذي أجازه أبو عثمان فاسد من قبل أنه لا يمتنع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p558/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p558/r5.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p558/r5.claim: The name Ḥaywa, as in Rajāʾ b. Ḥaywa, originally had a final yāʾ changed to wāw to avoid doubling; proper names permit such extensions.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p558/r5.anchor: وبهذا علمنا أن حيوة في مثل: رجاء بن حيوة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p560/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p560/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p560/r1.claim: If they understood, they would choose what lasts over what passes away; they do not understand.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p560/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: {لو كانوا يعلمون} يعني لو علموا لرغبوا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:29:63-67/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:29:63-67/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:29:63-67/r3.claim: This worldly life is diversion and play because it soon passes away, while the hereafter is lasting life; they fail to know that permanence.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:29:63-67/r3.anchor: لنفادها عن قريب { وإن الدار الآخرة لهي الحيوان } الحياة الدائمة

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p640/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p640/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p640/r5.claim: The worldly people meant here are the polytheists, who want nothing beyond this life and deny the afterlife.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p640/r5.anchor: أي: أن أهل الدنيا أهل لهو ولعب، يعني: المشركين هم أهل الدنيا الذين لا يريدون غيرها، لا يقرون بالآخرة.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p640/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p640/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p640/r6.claim: The hereafter meant here is Paradise.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p640/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p640/r7.speaker: ابن مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p640/r7.claim: Ibn Mujahid, from his father, says the afterlife is life without death: its inhabitants remain and never die.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p640/r7.anchor: ابن مجاهد، عن أبيه قال: لا موت فيها، أي: يبقى فيها أهلها لا يموتون.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p640/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p640/r8.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p640/r8.claim: If the polytheists knew the truth, they would know that the afterlife is better than this world.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p640/r8.anchor: يعني: المشركين، أي: لو كانوا يعلمون لعلموا أن الآخرة خير من الدنيا.

MAJAZ:v2p117/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p117/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p117/r1.claim: Al-ḥayawān means life, so the afterlife is life itself; the lām is emphatic, and ḥayawān and ḥayāh are nouns from ḥayiya, as al-ʿAjjāj’s line attests.
MAJAZ:v2p117/r1.anchor: الدار الآخرة لهي الحيوان» (64) مجازه: الدار الآخرة هى الحيوان، واللام تزاد للتوكيد، قال الشاعر:

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:64/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:64/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:64/r1.claim: Worldly attachment underlies the polytheists' position and also explains many other deniers' rejection.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:64/r1.anchor: Putperestlerin anılan tutumu benimsemelerinin temelinde dünya tutkusunun bulunduğuna işaret edilmektedir. Aslında bu durum birçok inkârcı için de geçerlidir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:64/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:64/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:64/r2.claim: Religion's commands and prohibitions constrain desire: people who follow reason and conscience integrate faith into their will, while those ruled by desire regard religious duties as burdens and adopt an anti-religious outlook.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:64/r2.anchor: aklının ve vicdanının buyruklarını nefsânî isteklerine hâkim kılanlar iradelerini inançlarıyla bütünleştirir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:64/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:64/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:64/r3.claim: The verse rejects a worldview that treats life as nothing more than ordinary, passing pleasures and delights.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:64/r3.anchor: bu anlayışla yaşanan bir dünyanın sadece sıradan, gelip geçici zevkler ve hazlardan ibaret olduğu uyarısında bulunmaktadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:64/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:64/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:64/r4.claim: What matters is securing the real life in the afterlife and working for its happiness and peace.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:64/r4.anchor: insan için önemli olan, “âhiret yurdu”ndaki asıl hayatı kurtarması, oradaki mutluluk ve esenliği için çalışmasıdır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:64/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:64/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:64/r5.claim: Devotion to enduring righteous deeds makes life meaningful in this world as well as preparing a person for the afterlife; the author cites Kahf 18:46.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:64/r5.anchor: hedefini dünyanın geçici zevkleriyle sınırlamayıp kendini “bâki kalan sâlih işler”e (Kehf 18/46) adadığı takdirde sadece âhireti için çalışmakla kalmayıp dünyasını da anlamlı kılmış olur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:64/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:64/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:64/r6.claim: The faithful recognize God as sole authority in every matter, worship and obey only Him, live by His will, and expect the good of both worlds from Him; with faith and sincerity they attain both.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:64/r6.anchor: din ve dünya ile ilgili bütün işlerinde Allah’ı tek ve mutlak otorite olarak görür, yalnız O’na kul olur

BURHAN:v1p120/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p120/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p120/r2.claim: Play usually precedes amusement because childhood play comes before youthful amusement; 57:20 maps these stages onto play, amusement, adornment, rivalry, and accumulation.
BURHAN:v1p120/r2.anchor: وإنما قدم اللعب فى الأكثر لأن اللعب زمان الصبا واللهو زمان الشباب وزمان الصبا متقدم على زمان اللهو

BURHAN:v1p120/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p120/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p120/r3.claim: In al-Aʿraf, amusement comes first because the passage concerns the Day of Judgment and orders the two states by what has just ended.
BURHAN:v1p120/r3.anchor: وقدم اللهو فى الأعراف لأن ذلك يوم القيامة فذكر على ترتيب ما انقضى

BURHAN:v1p120/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p120/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p120/r4.claim: In 29:64 both words describe worldly life’s brevity; amusement comes first because youth lasts longer than childhood play, while the afterlife is lasting life.
BURHAN:v1p120/r4.anchor: وأما العنكبوت فالمراد بذكرهما زمان الدنيا وأنه سريع الانقضاء قليل البقاء

BURHAN:v1p407#2/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p407#2/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p407#2/r2.claim: The incompleteness of worldly existence compared with the afterlife is illustrated by calling the latter the true life.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p730/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p730/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p730/r1.claim: The unusual order in 29:64 puts distraction before play because wealth and provision occasion diversion, as in the warning not to let wealth and children distract believers.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p730/r1.anchor: فالرزق ليس مدعاة اللعب وإنما مدعاة اللهو كما في قوله تعالى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p639/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p639/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p639/r1.claim: Al-hayawan is a verbal noun on the faʿalan pattern, like gathayan, fayadan, dawaran, and ghaliyan.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p639/r1.anchor: الحيوان: مصدر على وزن فعلان مثل غثيان وفيضان ودوران وغليان.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p639/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p639/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p639/r2.claim: The pattern conveys continuous movement and renewal: the afterlife is active, without sleep, while worldly life is like sleep beside it; hayat alone would suggest fluctuation, so hayawan fits.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p639/r2.anchor: صيغة في المصادر تدلّ على الحركة المستمرة والحدوث وهي أعلى أنواع الحياة
